item.title: Sub-Laplacian Comparison Theorem and Gradient Estimates on Complete Noncompact Contact Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.31720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we first derive the Bochner-type formulas of the Hermitian-Tanno connection on contact Riemannian manifolds. Second, we prove a sub-Laplacian comparison theorem on complete noncompact contact Riemannian manifolds with bounded geometric conditions. Finally, we obtain the gradient estimates of a positive eigenfunction on a complete noncompact contact Riemannian manifold which satisfies similar geometric conditions.
item.dc:creator: Guilin Yang, Biqiang Zhao, Weihao Zheng

item.title: The Calabi-Yau and Sullivan conjectures for minimal surfaces with symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.31847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite group acting on a connected open Riemann surface \(X\) by holomorphic automorphisms and acting on a Euclidean space \(\mathbb R^n\), \(n\ge 3\), by orthogonal transformations. In a previous paper, the second author gave a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a \(G\)-equivariant conformal minimal immersion \(F:X\to\mathbb R^n\), and he asked whether such \(F\) can be chosen to be a proper map. Assuming that this condition holds, we give an affirmative answer when \(X\) is a bordered Riemann surface and \(G\) acts freely on the boundary of \(X\). This contributes to the Sullivan conjecture concerning the existence of proper hyperbolic minimal surfaces in \(\mathbb R^3\) of finite topology. Under the same conditions, we also construct a \(G\)-equivariant proper conformal minimal immersion of \(X\) to the unit ball of \(\mathbb R^n\) which is complete in the induced metric, thereby opening a new direction in the Calabi--Yau theory regarding the study of complete bounded minimal surfaces. Analogous results hold for null curves in \(\mathbb C^n\).
item.dc:creator: Antonio Alarcon, Franc Forstneric

item.title: Geometric Quantities in Spray Geometry and Their Applications to Finsler Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.31896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we give an overview of several developments in spray geometry and provide some further interpretations of the geometric quantities that arise naturally in this subject. We discuss, in particular, the $S$-curvature, the $\chi$-curvature, and several notions of Ricci curvature for sprays. We rederive a number of identities relating these quantities and explain their applications to locally projectively flat sprays and to projectively related sprays. We also discuss applications to Finsler geometry, with emphasis on the $\chi$-curvature of a Finsler metric and on the inverse problem of determining whether a given spray is induced by a Finsler metric.
item.dc:creator: Benling Li, Zhongmin Shen

item.title: Minimal Surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with Three Planar Ends II: Symmetry and Nonexistence
item.description: arXiv:2610.32111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study complete minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with three embedded planar ends parallel to those of the union of the Lagrangian catenoid and the plane containing its waist circle. We prove that no such complete embedded minimal surface of genus $g\geq 2$ with finite total curvature admits at least $4(g+1)$ symmetries. This contrasts sharply with the genus-one case, where highly symmetric examples do exist and are uniquely determined up to scaling and rigid motion.
item.dc:creator: Jaehoon Lee, Eungbeom Yeon

item.title: Dirac eigenvalues and the hyper-hemispherical radius
item.description: arXiv:2610.32117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a connected compact Riemannian spin manifold with boundary, we prove an upper estimate for the smallest eigenvalue of the Dirac operator under the boundary condition associated with a chirality operator. This upper bound is expressed in terms of the hyper-hemispherical radius. Moreover, the upper bound is realized if and only if the manifold is a hemisphere. As an application, we get a scalar curvature rigidity result for the hemisphere in the case of Lipschitz maps whose differential has a prescribed trace-norm bound. Our estimate extends B\"ar's result for closed manifolds, where the upper bound is given in terms of hyperspherical radius.
item.dc:creator: Pengshuai Shi

item.title: The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
item.description: arXiv:2610.32320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Miura

item.title: Fuglede's theorem in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2610.32393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Fuglede-type quantitative isoperimetric inequality for the Pansu sphere, the conjectured isoperimetric set in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^1$. We show that, among suitable volume-preserving normal perturbations of the Pansu sphere that are small in a weighted $C^2$-norm, the difference between the sub-Riemannian perimeters of the perturbed and unperturbed regions is bounded below by a positive constant times the square of their $L^1$-distance. The proof is based on a Riemannian approximation argument with uniform estimates.
item.dc:creator: Davide Massenz, Roberto Monti, Juli\'an Pozuelo

item.title: Characterizations of the plane and the catenoid as capillary minimal surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that an annular capillary minimal surface outside the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with one complete embedded end and finite total curvature must be either part of the plane or part of the catenoid. The proofs are based on the use of the Weierstrass data through the Hopf differential and associated holomorphic functions. For a planar end, we control the second fundamental form, while for a catenoidal end, we analyze the Gauss map in more detail using the boundary condition. We also prove nonexistence results for annular free boundary minimal surfaces with one end asymptotic to the end of Enneper's surface, under appropriate conditions. Finally, we establish an exterior analogue of Choe's result on capillary minimal surfaces with vertices.
item.dc:creator: Eungbeom Yeon

item.title: Marked length spectrum and area of surfaces with Anosov geodesic flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.32489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: More than twenty years ago, Croke and Dairbekov showed that a negatively curved metric $g_0$ on a closed surface has minimal area among all negatively curved Riemannian metrics $g$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $g_0$. We show that the curvature assumption on the second metric can be removed and extend this result to reversible Finsler metrics. More precisely, we prove that a reversible Finsler metric $F_0$ on a closed surface whose geodesic flow is Anosov has minimal area among all reversible Finsler metrics $F$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $F_0$.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Cossarini, St\'ephane Sabourau

item.title: The Eguchi Construction Arises from Bi-Lagrangian Structures
item.description:
arXiv:2610.32539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new geometric interpretation of Eguchi's construction, which associates to a statistical divergence, an essential ingredient of Information Geometry, a statistical structure on a differentiable manifold. Our approach is based on bi-Lagrangian geometry. Building on the work of O.~E.~Barndorff-Nielsen and P.~E.~Jupp~\cite{Barndorff}, we show that a statistical divergence naturally induces a bi-Lagrangian structure, hence a para-K"ahler structure. Within this framework, the Riemannian metric $g^D$ and the pair of dual connections $(
abla^D,{}^*
abla^D)$ of Eguchi's construction are induced by the para-K"ahler structure: $g^D$ is the restriction to the diagonal of the para-K"ahler metric $G$ of signature $(d,d)$, while $
abla^D$ and ${}^*
abla^D$ are obtained, through the two natural projections, from the Bott connections of the two transverse Lagrangian foliations, which are themselves the restrictions of the Levi-Civita connection of $G$ (the Hess, K"unneth or bi-Lagrangian connection). This perspective shows that the statistical structure associated with a divergence is not merely the formal outcome of successive differentiations, but the manifestation of an underlying bi-Lagrangian geometry. Our approach thus provides an intrinsic and unified understanding of Eguchi's construction, highlights the connections between information geometry, symplectic geometry and para-K"ahler geometry, and opens new research perspectives at the interface of these fields.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Gnandi, St\'ephane Puechmorel

item.title: Local rigidity for the sharp Nash inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.32560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $V$ be a nonempty relatively compact open subset of a smooth Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ without boundary. We prove that $C_{\mathrm N}(V,g)\ge C_{\mathrm N}(\mathbb R^n)$ and $\int_V \mathrm{Sc}_g d\mu_g\ge0$ imply $\mathrm{Rm}_g=0$ on $V$, where $C_{\mathrm N}$ denotes the optimal constant in the Nash inequality and $\mathrm{Sc}_g$ denotes the scalar curvature. This improves an earlier rigidity result of Druet, Hebey, and Vaugon [Int. Math. Res. Not. (1999), no. 14, 735--779].
item.dc:creator: Liang Cheng, Zhenyu Lu

item.title: A complete K\"ahler metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ of nonnegative Ricci curvature with Euclidean volume growth and nonunique asymptotic cone
item.description: arXiv:2610.32734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct complete smooth K\"ahler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^n$ , $n\ge2$, with nonnegative Ricci curvature, Euclidean volume growth, and nonunique tangent cones at infinity. More generally, we prescribe the entire tangent cone set within a class of smooth Hopf cones, using a compact connected family of positive transverse Ricci forms on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We identify all metric blow-downs and their Ricci currents, compute the exact asymptotic volume ratio, and classify isometries between the model cones. In particular, the K\"ahler condition does not ensure uniqueness at infinity under nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, even in complex dimension two.
item.dc:creator: Jiwei Dai, Wancheng Zhang

item.title: Instability of mean curvature flow in expander coordinates
item.description: arXiv:2610.32819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study rotationally symmetric graphical solutions to mean curvature flow that are initially close to a homothetic reference expander, in particular near infinity. Based on a computer algebra aided proof, we show that under appropriate conditions, at large times, the solutions are closer to a different expander than to the reference expander.
item.dc:creator: Ben S. Lambert, Oliver C. Schn\"urer

item.title: Conformal geodesics and the hyperboloid at timelike infinity
item.description: arXiv:2610.30466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A description of scattering in asymptotically flat spacetimes that includes both radiation and massive asymptotic states requires control of the relation between null and timelike infinity. Motivated by this problem, we use the properties of conformal geodesics to construct an extended representation of timelike infinity in Minkowski spacetime. The construction exploits the fact that every non-null metric geodesic in an Einstein spacetime is, up to an explicit local reparametrisation, a conformal geodesic. It replaces the point $i^+$ by a hyperboloidal boundary $\mathcal{H}^+$ meeting future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ at a corner $\mathcal{C}^{+}$, while fixing the location of $\mathscr{I}^+$ in the associated conformal Gaussian gauge. In this gauge, we derive the equations governing massless scalar and spin-$2$ fields. In particular, we obtain a transport equation for the scalar field along future null infinity and analyse the asymptotic behaviour of its spherical-harmonic modes near timelike infinity. We also derive the explicit massless spin-$2$ equations in this gauge. Finally, we examine the relation to projective extensions and to the hyperbolic base of the extended Carrollian space $\mathrm{Ti}$. Our results provide a geometric framework for studying the connection between late-time and null asymptotics which is a prerequisite for scattering constructions relevant to flat space holography.
item.dc:creator: Achilleas V. Koukas, Mariem Magdy, Juan A. Valiente Kroon

item.title: On polarizations of affine Calabi--Yau varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.32036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(X, \Omega)$ be an affine Calabi--Yau variety, by which we mean a klt affine variety $X$ with a non-vanishing algebraic volume form $\Omega$. In connection with complete Calabi--Yau metrics of Euclidean volume growth on $(X, \Omega)$, we study algebraic aspects of polarizations of $X$ given by a negative valuation. We show that such a valuation is finitely generated with a klt degeneration if and only if $X$ admits a dlt log Fano type compactification, generalizing a compactification considered by Tian--Yau. We further give a valuative criterion detecting K-semistability of the degeneration by a negative valuation.
item.dc:creator: Yueqiao Wu

item.title: Group Actions on Aspherical Alexandrov Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conner and Raymond proved that if a connected, compact Lie group $G$ acts effectively on a closed aspherical manifold $M$, then $G$ is a torus and the fundamental group of $G$ injects into the center of $\pi_1(M)$. We prove the corresponding result for effective isometric actions on closed, aspherical Alexandrov spaces.
item.dc:creator: No\'e B\'arcenas, Jes\'us N\'u\~nez-Zimbr\'on

item.title: Gagliardo--Nirenberg extremals on manifolds with small holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.32173v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the sharp homogeneous Dirichlet Gagliardo--Nirenberg quotient on a closed Riemannian manifold with holes of small capacity and connected complements. For each fixed exponent $2<q<2^*$, the nonnegative $L^2$-normalized extremal exists and is unique when the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_D$ is sufficiently small. If the ambient volume is $V$ and $\beta=n(q-2)/2$, the sharp constant satisfies $C_D=V^{1-q/2}\lambda_D^{-\beta/2}(1+O(\lambda_D))$. For the normalized first eigenfunction $\varphi_D$, we obtain $\|u_D-\varphi_D\|_{H^1}=O(\lambda_D^{3/2})$ and $C_D/W_{M_D}(\varphi_D)=1+O(\lambda_D^2)$, together with a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the relative deficit. The constants depend only on the ambient manifold and the exponent. On general compact manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions, we prove compactness above the Euclidean sharp constant and describe concentration at equality. Positive scalar curvature at one interior point implies attainment. For the $L^2$-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger energy, the mass threshold for negative energy tends to zero as the capacity of the holes tends to zero, whereas the threshold for unboundedness below is unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Utsab Sarkar

item.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
item.description: arXiv:2610.32707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$ -\Delta u=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0 \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, \tag*{$(*)$} $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that problem $(*)$ admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove compactness of the solution set of $(*)$ by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is nondegenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set of $(*)$ is finite. Our results give a negative answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].
item.dc:creator: Wei Ji, Yixing Pu

item.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollob\'as and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Guti\'errez, Bernu\'es, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollob\'as and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Luis J. Al\'ias, Bernardo Gonz\'alez Merino, Beatriz Mar\'in Gimeno

item.title: Envelopes of Horospheres and Weingarten Surfaces in Hyperbolic 3-Space
item.description: arXiv:2401.12115v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive basic differential geometric formulae for surfaces in hyperbolic space represented as envelopes of horospheres. The dual notion of parallel hypersurfaces is also studied. The representation is applied to prove existence and regularity theorems for Weingarten surfaces in H^3, which satisfy (1-a)K = a(2-H), for an a < 0, and have a specified boundary curve at infinity. These surfaces are shown to be closely connected to conformal mappings of domains in S^2 into the unit disk and provide Riemannian interpretations for some conformal invariants associated to such mappings. This paper was originally written in 1984, before I learned to use TeX, and was typed by one of the secretaries in the Princeton Math Department. It was more or less, my first original work after my dissertation. For some reason, I was not able to get this paper published in a timely manner. The results and perspective in this paper have proved to be useful to a variety of people, some of whom asked me to render the article into TeX and post it to the arXiv. I had been seriously thinking about doing this, when Martin Bridgeman sent me a transcription of my original article into TeX. I am extremely grateful to him for the effort he has put into this project. The paper is now formatted in a more or less modern AMS-article style, but for lots of additional punctuation, a few corrections and some minor stylistic changes, the content has been largely reproduced as it originally was. Remarks about the 'state-of-the-art' in hyperbolic geometry are obviously way out of date, as there has been enormous progress in many aspects of this still rich subject.
item.dc:creator: Charles L. Epstein

item.title: Symmetries and Higher-Form Connections in Derived Differential Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2602.03441v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a general definition of higher-form connections on principal $\infty$-bundles in differential geometry. These connections are built as infinitesimal parallel transports and thus satisfy the fake-curvature condition. We achieve this by developing the formal differentiation and integration of maps from smooth manifolds to derived stacks with sufficient deformation theory. That allows us to introduce the Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid of a principal $\infty$-bundle and establish its global sections as the $L_\infty$-algebra of the derived higher symmetry group of the bundle. We define the space of $p$-form connections on an $\infty$-bundle as the space of order $p$ splittings of its Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid. This can be cast equivalently as lifting the classifying map of a bundle on a manifold to the order $p$ truncation of the de Rham stack of the manifold. We demonstrate that our new concept of derived geometric $p$-form connections recovers the known notion of connections on higher U(1)-bundles defined via \v{C}ech-Deligne differential cocycles. We further relate the $L_\infty$-algebras of derived higher symmetries of higher U(1)-bundles and higher Courant algebroids. Some applications in higher gauge theory and in supergravity are mentioned.
item.dc:creator: Severin Bunk, Lukas M\"uller, Joost Nuiten, Richard J. Szabo

item.title: Height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves
item.description: arXiv:2608.19517v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce families of Lagrange functions associated with height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves. We show that degeneracies of these families characterize geometric properties of the curves, such as inflections and vertices, and give geometric interpretations of the corresponding Lagrange multipliers in terms of contact with lines and circles.
item.dc:creator: Masaru Hasegawa

item.title: Hyperbolic Monge-Amp\`ere Equation on a Cylinder: Well-Posedness and Stability
item.description: arXiv:2509.25553v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper develops a rigorous analytic framework for the hyperbolic Monge-Amp\`ere equation on strip-like domains, which model wrinkled patterns in thin elastic sheets. Our work addresses the rigid side of the classical rigidity-flexibility dichotomy by defining this regime not by high smoothness, but by the more fundamental property of partial convexity. The hodograph transformation is the natural tool for this setting, as its validity is predicated on partial convexity. It converts the nonlinear Monge-Amp\`ere equation into a linear damped wave equation, allowing us to formulate a well-posed Cauchy-Goursat problem. A key challenge is the corner singularity that arises where characteristic and non-characteristic boundary data meet. To resolve this, we develop a parametrix-corrector decomposition that captures the solution's inherent singular behavior. This method recasts the problem as a singular Volterra integral equation, for which we prove the existence and uniqueness of a new class of hodograph weak solutions. Finally, we derive energy estimates to establish the quantitative stability of these rigid solutions under perturbations of the underlying curvature function.
item.dc:creator: Maria Deliyianni, Shankar C. Venkataramani

item.title: Convex Analysis of Relaxation Dynamics in Chemical Reaction Networks and Generalized Gradient Flows
item.description: arXiv:2602.18932v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain bounds on the Kullback--Leibler divergence to equilibrium for mass-action chemical reaction networks (CRNs) with equilibrium. The associated trajectory-dependent bounds are characterized in terms of the singular values of the stoichiometric matrix, convexity parameters, and time-integrated activities via deformed-exponential-type functions. We further extend these bounds within a generalized gradient flow framework. We highlight the biological relevance of this framework: the resulting bounds apply to quasi-steady-state regimes, where long transients and plateau-like behavior are common and functionally important. We illustrate the framework using a catalytic CRN exhibiting plateaus, where the bounds provide an a posteriori characterization of slow relaxation induced by local convexity and provide a bound-based approach to quantifying relaxation in CRNs.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Sugie, Dimitri Loutchko, Tetsuya J. Kobayashi

item.title: Symmetry Breaking and Moduli for Ancient Yamabe Flows on the Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2606.22355v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every $n\ge3$, we construct compact Type II ancient Yamabe flows in the round conformal class of the unit $n$-sphere $\Ss^n$. After stereographic projection and rescaling of time and conformal factor, the solutions are asymptotic backward in time to finite superpositions of Aubin--Talenti bubbles with mutually comparable scales. For integers $h\ge1$ and $k\ge2$, the limiting centers form $h$ coaxial regular $k$-gons; when $h\ge2$, their distinct layer heights may be prescribed arbitrarily in the interval $(-1,1)$. If $hk\ge3$, the resulting flows are not geometrically equivalent to any rotationally symmetric ancient flow. For each flow, there is a fixed point of $\Ss^n$ at which the Ricci tensor has both positive and negative eigenvalues on every time slice. The corresponding volume-normalized Yamabe flows are also ancient. After rescaling each time slice to a fixed volume, the metrics converge to a wedge of $hk$ isometric round $n$-spheres in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology, as time tends to $-\infty$. For fixed $h,k\ge2$, the concentration configurations admit an explicit $(h-1)$-parameter description up to M\"obius transformations. Consequently, the construction yields geometrically inequivalent flows indexed by a nonempty open subset of $\R^{h-1}$, all with the same fixed-volume backward Gromov--Hausdorff limit. The proof uses inner--outer gluing for the quasilinear parabolic equation in $n$-dimensional space that exhibits Kelvin symmetry. Weighted Euclidean and spherical H\"older estimates control the nonlinear terms and, together with parabolic regularity, yield smooth extension of the conformal metrics across the north pole of $\Ss^n$.
item.dc:creator: Haixia Chen, Seunghyeok Kim, Monica Musso

item.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
item.description: arXiv:2610.27263v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.
item.dc:creator: Andre M. Sonnet, Epifanio G. Virga
